facts.statement: The genus Aztecodus was described by Long and Young in 1995.
Aztecodus was an extinct cartilaginous fish that lived during the Devonian period.
facts.quote: Aztecodus is an extinct genus of Chondrichthyian from the Devonian period.

facts.statement: The genus is named after the Aztec Siltstone found in southern Victoria Land, Antarctica.
facts.quote: It is named for middle to late Devonian-aged Aztec Siltstone of southern Victoria Land, Antarctica which produces this genus.

facts.statement: The only known species is A. harmsenae, named in honor of sedimentologist Dr. Fraka Harmsen.
facts.quote: It currently contains a singular species, A. harmsenae. It is named for sedimentologist Dr. Fraka Harmsen.

facts.statement: Aztecodus possessed unique broad teeth with widely divergent cusps and a crenulated cutting edge.
facts.quote: It has unique teeth which are broad with widely divergent cusps separated by a crenulated cutting edge.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Anareodus statei is a junior synonym of Aztecodus harmsenae.
facts.quote: Anareodus statei may be a junior synonym to this genus and species.
